title: Preparing Phytoplankton Samples for Elemental Carbon and Nitrogen Analysis
author: Jana Hinners

steps.title: Prepare and Precombust Filters
steps.instruction: Prepare Whatman GFF filters for analysis by removing organic contaminants and recording initial weights.

substeps.instruction: Wrap up to 20 Whatman GFF filters in aluminium foil.
Weigh precombusted filters and store them individually and labelled (e.g., in 6-well microtitre plates).

steps.title: Cultivate Phytoplankton
steps.instruction: Grow phytoplankton cultures to the appropriate growth phase.

substeps.instruction: Grow 45 mL phytoplankton cultures in 50 mL flasks until they reach mid-exponential phase (indicated by visible colour).

steps.title: Perform Cell Counting
steps.instruction: Remove a small aliquot of each sample for cell quantification.

substeps.instruction: Use 1 mL of each sample for cell counting (e.g., using a fluorescence plate reader, FlowCam, FlowCytometry, or microscopy).

steps.title: Filter Phytoplankton Samples
steps.instruction: Concentrate the phytoplankton biomass onto the precombusted GFF filters using vacuum filtration.

substeps.instruction: From the remaining 44 mL per sample, use 20 mL for each of 2 replicate filters.
Apply the sample onto the filter using a pipette, carefully checking the volume.
Wash the edge of the filter unit and the filter with 10 mL distilled water.

steps.title: Dry and Weigh Biomass
steps.instruction: Remove moisture from the filters to determine the net dry biomass weight.

substeps.instruction: Store filters with biomass in 6-well plates and let them dry with a loose lid overnight.
Weigh all dried filters again and calculate the net weight of the dry biomass for each filter.

steps.title: Remove Inorganic Carbon
steps.instruction: Treat filters to remove inorganic carbon if using an elemental analyzer that measures total carbon content.

substeps.instruction: Soak filters with 200 µL distilled water (can be done in 6-well plates).
Apply 100 µL 2M HCl onto each filter.
